cases.description: Octet is negative; first condition (octet >= 0) fails, method should short‑circuit and return false.
Octet is within the range of the decode table length, but the decode table entry at that index is -1, causing the final condition to fail and the method to return false.
Octet is greater than or equal to decodeTable.length (decodeTable length is 8). The second condition fails, method returns false.
Octet is non‑negative, less than decodeTable.length, and decodeTable[octet] is not -1. All conditions are satisfied, method should return true.
Lowest non‑negative octet; NUL (0) is not part of the Base64 alphabet, so decodeTable[0] == -1 and the method returns false.
Octet corresponds to ASCII 'A', the first character of the standard Base64 alphabet; decodeTable[65] != -1, method returns true.
Octet is ASCII '@', which is not in the Base64 alphabet; decodeTable[64] == -1, method returns false.
Octet is ASCII 'z', a valid Base64 alphabet character; decodeTable[122] != -1, method returns true.
Octet is ASCII '+', a valid Base64 alphabet character; decodeTable[43] != -1, method returns true.
Octet is the highest index within the typical decode table (127); DEL character is not in the alphabet, decodeTable[127] == -1, method returns false.
Minimum byte value; negative octet fails the first condition (octet >= 0) and the method returns false.
Octet -1 (0xFF) is negative; first condition fails, method returns false.
decodeTable field is deliberately set to null (e.g., via reflection) before invoking isInAlphabet; accessing decodeTable.length causes a NullPointerException.
